subject: "Data not in the same coordinate system"

messages.author: 9eada87ac9c1c9b2
messages.subject: "Data not in the same coordinate system"
parts:
Hello everyone,

First, I'd like to thank everyone for the great discussions I have been reading in this group! They have been very enlightening. 

I am currently fitting akdes to highly irregularly sampled VHF data from 16 territorial forest songbirds that we tracked this summer. I have had no trouble producing UDs on 15 of the 16 birds, but the function consistently fails for the last bird, giving me the following error:

Warning: Fit object returned. DOF[area] = 4.85145214203012e-07Error in akde(data[SUB], CTMM[SUB], VMM = VMM[SUB], R = R, SP = SP, SP.in = SP.in, : Data not in single coordinate system.

I have gone through the csv line-by-line for this bird and found no erroneous coordinates. The entire csv is in decimal degrees. Does anyone have any idea what may be causing this issue?

Thanks,
Tyler

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: "Data not in the same coordinate system"
parts:
Hi Tyler,

The usual culprit for the warning is that the individual wasn't resident during the sampling period. What does the variogram look like? What does the track look like, when colored by time?

The error would be caused by the projection of the tracking data and the model fit not all matching. What do projection(data) and projection(CTMM) return?

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 9eada87ac9c1c9b2
messages.subject: Re: "Data not in the same coordinate system"
parts:
Hello Chris,

Ah, that would make sense! Although most displayed range residency behavior, a few of the birds definitely displayed non-stationary behavior during different periods of the breeding cycle (e.g., slightly shifting ranges a couple hundred meters during second nesting attempts or the post-fledging and post-breeding periods). I planned to split up the locations by time of season or behavior at some point, but I was trying to force the full-season AKDEs for comparison's/exploration's sake and for practice while I find my way around ctmm. 

Strangely, the projection() function indicates that both the data and fit objects have the same reference coordinates and projections (wgs84). 

I had a very irregular sampling interval. At its core, I did two-minute burst sampling (see Barg et al. 2005) for 30 minutes every other day, with sessions alternating between morning and afternoon to help account for any temporal variation in space use. However, depending on the bird's behavior, the sampling interval ranged between as little as two minutes to as long as 30 minutes during the session window (sometimes we were only able to get a single location on a bird during the session). Additionally, I wasn't always able to track each bird every other day due to logistics and equipment malfunctions, especially early and late in the season. As a result, my variograms are quite messy (see below for the variogram for this particular bird), although I am sure there is an easy way to clean them up with the dt argument. 



Thanks!

Best,
Tyler

messages.subject: Re: "Data not in the same coordinate system"
parts:
Hi Tyler,

That sounds like dt=c(2%#%'min',30%#%'min')

If you are getting that error with identical projections, then if you can make a minimal working example (data + script) for me, I will take a look at it.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: "Data not in the same coordinate system"
parts:
Hi Tyler,

You are running ctmm.select() with verbose=TRUE, which returns a list of all candidate models. Then you are feeding the whole list to akde() with just one tracking dataset. There needs to be one (best) model per tracking dataset.
I will improve the error message.

Best,
Chris
